batches.title: Quinoa, Beef Mince (Mediterranean), Roasted Bell Peppers & Green Lentils
steps: Cook quinoa: rinse 500 g dry quinoa under cold water 1 minute. Place in a large pot with 1 L cold salted water. Bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer, cover and cook 15 minutes until water is absorbed. Fluff with fork. Spread on a baking tray to cool quickly. Divide into 6 portions (~130 g each) in airtight containers; label and refrigerate.

Brown beef mince (Mediterranean): heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add 600 g beef mince; break apart with a wooden spoon. Cook 6–8 minutes until no pink remains. Add 2 cloves minced garlic, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp paprika, 1 tsp oregano, ½ tsp sea salt; stir 2 minutes. Remove from heat; cool completely on a plate. Portion into 2 containers: 260 g (2 × Monday/Thursday Diego) and 180 g (2 × Monday/Thursday Diana); refrigerate.

Roast bell peppers: slice 6 bell peppers (mixed colours) into strips; toss in a bowl with 2 tbsp olive oil, 1 tsp paprika, ½ tsp sea salt, ½ tsp black pepper. Spread on 2 lined baking trays in a single layer. Roast at 200 °C (fan) for 25 minutes until edges are charred. Cool completely; transfer to 2 airtight containers; refrigerate.

Prepare green lentils: open 2 × 400 g cans green lentils; drain and rinse under cold water. Transfer to a bowl; season with 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp olive oil, ½ tsp sea salt; stir to coat. Portion into 2 containers for Monday and Thursday; refrigerate.

Brown beef mince (Mexican tacos): heat 1 tbsp olive oil in the same pan over medium-high. Add 400 g beef mince; break apart. Cook 5 minutes; add 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp chilli powder, 1 tsp garlic powder, ½ tsp oregano, ½ tsp sea salt; stir 2 minutes. Cool completely; portion into 2 containers for Tuesday dinner; refrigerate.
Prepare black beans (Tuesday dinner): drain and rinse 1 × 400 g can black beans. Toss with ½ tsp cumin, ½ tsp lime juice, pinch of salt. Store in a small container in the fridge.
yields: Mexican spiced beef mince: ~350 g cooked

day_of_assembly.Monday: Lunch — Mediterranean Beef & Lentil Bowl: reheat 130 g (Diego) / 90 g (Diana) quinoa in microwave 90 sec; reheat beef portion and lentils in pan 4 min; warm bell peppers 45 sec in microwave; assemble bowl and drizzle with olive oil and balsamic vinegar.
day_of_assembly.Tuesday: Dinner — Mexican Beef & Black Bean Tacos: reheat Mexican beef in pan 4 min; warm black beans with lime juice 1 min; warm tortillas in dry pan; fill tortillas with beef, beans, bell pepper strips; dress spinach with olive oil and balsamic vinegar on the side.
day_of_assembly.Thursday: ⚠ Cook fresh today — do NOT use the Sunday batch (red meat is only safe ~3 day(s); this is day 4).

storage.safety_note: Store in coldest part of fridge. Reheat to 74 °C before serving.

batches.title: Beef Chuck Stew & Roasted Zucchini
steps: Cube beef chuck: trim and cut 700 g beef chuck into 3 cm cubes. Pat dry with kitchen paper — this helps browning.

Brown the chuck: heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over high heat. Add beef cubes in 2 batches (do not crowd the pan); sear 2–3 minutes per side until a deep brown crust forms. Remove batches to a plate.

Build the stew base: lower heat to medium; add 3 cloves minced garlic to the pot; cook 30 seconds. Add 2 tbsp tomato paste; stir 1 minute. Pour in 500 ml water (or beef stock if available). Add 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp paprika, 1 tsp oregano, ½ tsp thyme, 1 tsp sea salt, ½ tsp black pepper; stir well.

Braise: return beef cubes to the pot; bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to low; cover and simmer 60 minutes, stirring occasionally, until beef is fork-tender. Add a splash of water if the liquid reduces too much.
Cool and portion: remove pot from heat; let cool 15 minutes with lid off. Portion into 4 containers (2 × Wednesday lunch, 2 × Thursday lunch, labelled by day and person). Refrigerate immediately.

Roast zucchini: while stew simmers, slice 3 zucchini (600 g total) into half-moon pieces. Toss with 1 tbsp olive oil, 1 tsp oregano, ½ tsp garlic powder, ½ tsp sea salt. Spread on 2 lined baking trays. Roast at 200 °C for 20 minutes until golden. Cool; store in 1 large container in fridge (used Wednesday and Thursday lunch).
yields: Braised beef chuck stew: ~550 g cooked (4 portions — enough for Wed & Thu lunches for 2 people)
Roasted zucchini: ~400 g (2 portions per day over Wed & Thu)

day_of_assembly.Wednesday: Lunch — French-Style Beef & Chickpea Stew with Sweet Potato: reheat 150 g (Diego) / 110 g (Diana) beef chuck stew in a saucepan 5–6 min; stir in chickpeas 2 min; reheat baked sweet potato in microwave 2 min; serve stew alongside sweet potato with balsamic vinegar.
day_of_assembly.Thursday: ⚠ Cook fresh today — do NOT use the Sunday batch (red meat is only safe ~3 day(s); this is day 4).

storage.safety_note: Store in coldest part of fridge. Reheat to 74 °C before serving.

batches.title: Baked Sweet Potatoes (for Wednesday & Thursday lunches)
steps: Preheat oven to 200 °C. Scrub 5 medium sweet potatoes (each ~180 g) under running water; pierce each 4–5 times with a fork.
Place directly on the oven rack or a baking tray. Bake 40–45 minutes until a fork slides in easily and the skin is slightly wrinkled.
Remove from oven; allow to cool completely at room temperature (~20 minutes). Do NOT wrap in foil while cooling — this traps steam and makes the skin soggy.
Once cool, place in 2 separate airtight containers or zip-lock bags; label with day. Refrigerate immediately. Use within 4 days.
yields: 5 baked sweet potatoes (~900 g total cooked weight), used for Wednesday and Thursday lunches

day_of_assembly.Wednesday: Lunch — French-Style Beef & Chickpea Stew with Sweet Potato: reheat 1 whole sweet potato (Diego, 180 g) or ¾ (Diana, 130 g) in microwave 2 min; serve alongside beef-chickpea stew.
day_of_assembly.Thursday: Lunch — Mediterranean Beef Chuck & Lentil Skillet: no sweet potato used Thursday — roasted zucchini replaces it in this dish. Remaining sweet potatoes reserved for weekend or discard if past 4-day window.

storage.safety_note: Cooked vegetables store well. Roasted veg can be eaten cold in salads.
